svg.text: Figure 4.2 — Query sequence (origin path and cached repeat)

g.text: 3. tier-1 miss → probe shared L2 row cache#<hash> (~5–15 ms) · HIT-L2 ⇒ backfill L1, respond
5. vector search, top 2×k; metadata (text, filename) rides with each vector
6. batch-get job rows; keep only COMPLETED (live) documents — expired chunks can never be cited
7. numbered excerpts [1..k] → grounded prompt → generate answer (gemma, ≈2.5 s)
8. cache-ahead-of-response: write L2 row (TTL 1 h) and L1 entry BEFORE responding
9. 200 OK {answer, sources[], cache:"MISS", latencyMs} — X-Cache: MISS
10. repeat (or another user asks the same question)
11. tier-1 hit — no network hop at all

svg.text: • The cache KEY = hash(normalised question | topK | corpus version). The version marker invalidates every answer when the corpus changes, so stale citations cannot survive an upload or an expiry sweep.
• Over-fetching (2×k) plus the live-job filter means the k excerpts actually used are chosen AFTER expiry/state checking — retrieval correctness is decoupled from storage cleanup timing.
• Cache-ahead-of-response: if the HTTP response is lost after generation, the retry is a cache hit — failures at the edge become free retries instead of expensive re-generation.
• The response always reports tier and latency (X-Cache + latencyMs), which is what the UI badge renders and what the cache experiment measured.
Observed: origin ≈2 663 ms end-to-end (embed + search + filter + generate) · cached ≈0 ms at L1 · L2 ≈5–15 ms when the shared row serves a cold instance.
Answer contract: answers are grounded ONLY in retrieved excerpts; when excerpts do not contain the answer the model is instructed to say so, rather than fall back to general knowledge.
Concurrency: API instances share nothing (stateless); tier 1 is per-instance, tier 2 is global — warm instances hit L1, cold instances still hit L2, both skip all model calls.
